He intimately recalls the trauma of watching that delicate system fracture under Indira Gandhi's centralizing impulse and the declaration of the Emergency, an epoch that compelled him to turn decisively toward civil liberties activism and alternative politics. In contemporary political debates, whenever observers proclaim the birth of a 'New BJP System' or a structural single-party hegemony under Narendra Modi, Kothari recalls his original thesis, offering sharp comparative reflections on how today's ideological homogenization and centralized command fundamentally diverge from the porous, self-correcting consensus mechanisms that once defined the early Indian republic.
